title: 2017 AMC 12B 16
statement: The number \(21!\) \(= 51{,}090{,}942{,}171{,}709{,}440{,}000\) has over \(60{,}000\) positive integer divisors. One of them is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is odd?

solutions.text:
The exponent of \(2\) in \(21!\) is \(\lfloor \frac{21}{2} \rfloor\) \(+ \lfloor \frac{21}{4} \rfloor\) \(+ \lfloor \frac{21}{8} \rfloor\) \(+ \lfloor \frac{21}{16} \rfloor\) \(= 10 + 5 + 2 + 1\) \(= 18.\) Every divisor has the form \(2^i b\) with \(0 \le i \le 18\) and \(b\) odd; it is odd exactly when \(i = 0.\) So the fraction of odd divisors is \(\dfrac{1}{18 + 1} = \dfrac{1}{19}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Find the exponent of \(2\) in \(21!\) using \(\lfloor \frac{21}{2} \rfloor + \lfloor \frac{21}{4} \rfloor + \cdots\)
A divisor is odd iff it uses \(2^0.\) With exponent \(e,\) the odd divisors are a fraction \(\dfrac{1}{e+1}\) of all divisors
